item.title: MORRISETTE: Tariff Whiplash and a Rising Black Recession
item.description: Black unemployment has reached its highest level in four years due to the Trump Administration's targeted dismantling of equity programs and the imposition of new tariffs, resulting in a Black recession. The post MORRISETTE: Tariff Whiplash and a Rising Black Recession appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Civil Rights Leaders Demand End to $2.13 Tipped Wage, Call It a Legacy of Slavery
item.description: Justice, political and labor leaders gathered in New York to call for the passage of Living Wage for All legislation, which would raise the minimum wage to $30 an hour in New York and $25 an hour federally, and eliminate all subminimum wages, in order to address the racial and gender wage gaps exacerbated by the federal tipped wage of $2.13 an hour. The post Civil Rights Leaders Demand End to $2.13 Tipped Wage, Call It a Legacy of Slavery appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Snow, Wind and Cancellations Paralyze D.C. as Nor’easter Roars Up East Coast
item.description: Winter Storm Hernando brought heavy snow and powerful wind gusts to the mid-Atlantic, causing flight cancellations, rail service disruptions, and power outages for tens of thousands. The post Snow, Wind and Cancellations Paralyze D.C. as Nor’easter Roars Up East Coast appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Inside Out: A View of Hope from Incarceration
item.description: The Lorton Prison photography program, which ran from 1980 to 1989, offered incarcerated men a creative outlet to express themselves and connect to the outside world, and now their photos are being showcased in the exhibition "Inside Out: Dignity and the Art of Seeing" at the DC Commission on the Arts and Humanities. The post Inside Out: A View of Hope from Incarceration appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Milk & Honey Turns Dining Into Impact With Divine Nine Initiative
item.description: Thompson Restaurants' Milk & Honey brand is partnering with D.C.'s Divine Nine network to raise funds for scholarships and service efforts, with diners able to contribute by rounding up their checks and participating in the Black Love Dine & Donate Day. The post Milk & Honey Turns Dining Into Impact With Divine Nine Initiative appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: MALVEAUX: The Rotunda Is Too Small for Rev. Jesse Jackson
item.description: The Rev. Jesse Jackson's legacy of fighting for justice and equality is too great to be contained by the Capitol Rotunda, and his life of disruption and struggle should be remembered for its impact on American democracy. The post MALVEAUX: The Rotunda Is Too Small for Rev. Jesse Jackson appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DC Jazz Fest Sets the Stage With 2026 Lineup
item.description: The 2026 DC JazzFest will be held from Sept. 2-6, featuring headliners such as Dee Dee Bridgewater, Joshua Redman, Kurt Elling and Nate Smith, as well as rising and homegrown talent, and will celebrate the historic impact of jazz over the course of America's 250 years. The post DC Jazz Fest Sets the Stage With 2026 Lineup appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: ABC Wraps Monthlong Campaign Screening Thousands for Heart Risks Nationwide
item.description: Despite advances in cardiovascular care, African Americans still die at higher rates due to heart disease, with hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and geography all playing a role in the disparity.
